source.title: Understanding Batch Normalization
source.authors: Johan Bjorck; C. Gomes; B. Selman; K. Weinberger

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether batch normalization changes training speed and tolerable learning rates using CIFAR-10 ResNet experiments; it does not reproduce the original BN study's exact experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training and testing accuracy curves for 110-layer ResNets under several learning rates, but the curve values are figure-only. It also reports the largest tested learning rate that avoids divergence for a BN network.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares training speed and viable learning rates with and without BN in a new setting: CIFAR-10 ResNet-110. It is not an original source for V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that BN's benefits are mainly mediated by larger learning rates, which accelerate convergence and increase SGD's implicit regularization. They argue that BN prevents activation growth during large updates and connect unnormalized networks' ill-behaved gradients to random initialization. The proposed generalization mechanism is an interpretation rather than a directly established sharp-minimum result.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares BN and non-BN CIFAR10 ResNet training and tests learning-rate schedules, rather than reproducing the original BN paper's experiments across sigmoid MNIST, VGG CIFAR-10, and Inception ImageNet.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes the outcome: low-rate BN is comparable to the unnormalized network, while higher-rate BN improves test accuracy and tolerates larger rates. Network depth and update frequency of normalization statistics also affect the maximum viable learning rate, as discussed in the text and appendices.

fits_no_version.finding: At matching low learning rates, BN and unnormalized networks have comparable test accuracy; higher-rate BN has better test accuracy and a smaller train-test gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Much of BN's generalization advantage in this setting is mediated by the learning rate it permits.

fits_no_version.finding: Gaussian matrix products become increasingly ill-conditioned with depth, and unnormalized ResNets exhibit uneven activation and gradient scales at initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Variance scaling alone need not ensure well-conditioned deep-network initialization.

record.code_released: not stated; code available upon request to the first author, with public release described as planned for a later date.
record.peer_reviewed: 32nd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2018), Montréal, Canada
record.problems: Accuracy values for the main BN and non-BN comparisons are shown in figures rather than stated numerically. The paper reports five-run means and standard deviations for Figure 1, but does not provide numeric accuracy values in the text. The experiments focus on CIFAR10 ResNets.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results bearing on a tested version were left out. Other measured quantities, such as gradient distributions, activation moments, and random-matrix singular values, do not measure the behaviors named by these claim versions.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error is not recoverable from the supplied curves. Random labels, CIFAR-100, model-size effects, and early-stopping effects are not tested.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain networks versus residual networks across depth, and the specified initialization remedies.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons measuring learning speed or trainable depth, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian tanh training, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional training.
Initial linearized stability thresholds, curvature reduction during recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence from below a measured threshold.
The named MNIST, VGG, and Inception settings; Fixup; and a readable matched-low-rate comparison of convergence speed.

missing.what: Explicit convergence schedules and the high-rate unnormalized failure: full BN trains at 0.1 over 165 epochs; without BN, 0.1 fails and convergence requires 0.0001 with roughly 2400 epochs. BN at 0.003 uses 1320 epochs.
BN only at the network top permits learning rate 0.03 and training over 330 epochs. This measures how much speed and tolerance can be retained with sparse normalization.

Component ablations: full mean-and-variance normalization, with or without affine parameters, uses 0.1 and 165 epochs; variance-only uses 0.01 and 330 epochs; mean-only uses 0.003 and 330 epochs; no components uses 0.0001 and 2640 epochs. These are selected training schedules, not exact stability thresholds.

Alternating normalization permits only 0.01; an unnormalized network warmed up for one epoch at 0.0001 subsequently permits 0.01. These qualify the role of normalization frequency and the initial training state in learning-rate tolerance.
BN diverges at learning rate 10.0, providing the tested upper failure alongside nondivergence at 3.0.

record.verdict_notes: Only supplied text was used. The extracted Figure 1 curves do not provide readable accuracy values. Equal final test accuracy under a matched schedule does not by itself justify a verdict against faster training, so the record's matched-low-rate limits_scope label is not retained.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random or corrupted labels and the effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of student width.
Plain versus residual networks as depth increases; the experiments use ResNets and do not test plain-network depth degradation or the stated remedies.
Comparisons of initialization schemes and their effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Training above the stability limit, curvature or sharpness dynamics, recovery, and divergence from below that limit.

Tests CIFAR-10 ResNets with and without BN and reports learning-curve comparisons and learning-rate tolerance. Does not test sigmoid MNIST, VGG CIFAR-10, Inception ImageNet, Santurkar et al.'s experiments, or Fixup.
